claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading is governed by interface-mediated dislocation activation in HEA nanoscale multilayers.
Severe lattice distortion enhances interface-mediated dislocation activation.
Localized short-range-order differences between adjacent layers enhance interface-mediated dislocation activation.
The proposed coating can contain alternating FCC/BCC HEA layers or multiple BCC HEA layers with different degrees of lattice distortion and short-range order.
Room-temperature or moderately elevated-temperature constant loading activates time-dependent plastic deformation while preserving multilayer thickness and composition.
Differences in lattice distortion and short-range order at layer interfaces create locally enhanced barriers to dislocation motion.
High lattice distortion in compositionally complex layers produces heterogeneous stress distributions.
Heterogeneous stresses caused by lattice distortion facilitate localized dislocation nucleation and pile-up at layer interfaces.
Dislocation accumulation at interfaces enhances interface slip.
Preferential dislocation accumulation and propagation along interfaces promote progressive plastic deformation under constant load.
HEA multilayers with greater lattice distortion will accumulate plastic strain faster than lower-distortion multilayers under identical creep conditions.
More highly distorted layers will exhibit greater defect density and local plastic flow.
Higher-distortion HEA multilayers will display observable interface slip or dislocation pile-ups.
Conventional or lower-distortion multilayers deform through mechanisms that are less interface-governed.
The proposed behavior is significant only while layer thickness remains nanoscale.
The proposed behavior is limited to loading and temperature regimes that activate time-dependent dislocation processes.
At extreme temperatures or after degradation of the multilayer architecture, mechanisms other than interface-mediated dislocation processes may dominate.
Mechanical properties and deformation mechanisms in HEAs can depend on temperature.

The hypothesis is falsified if higher-distortion samples do not show a significantly higher deformation rate or distinct interface dislocation structures relative to lower-distortion controls under identical conditions.
